messages:
Alex Chen: Hey team — just got an escalation from a customer using the TypeScript SDK streaming iterator. They say the stream sometimes returns partial content, then a duplicate chunk after a reconnect, and sometimes we bill them twice for essentially the same output. Repro steps attached below.

Priya Nair: Thanks Alex. Any error logs from the client or server? Is this auth/token-related?

Alex Chen: Customer sent client logs and a tiny repro. TL;DR: they run `for await (const chunk of client.streamCompletion(req)) { /* assemble */ }` and they have an auth refresh hook that rotates the token on 401. On token refresh we currently create a new EventSource connection and resume the iterator.

Samir Patel: That resume behavior rings a bell. We had a race where the SDK emits the leftover buffered chunk after a reconnect, then the server re-sends the same partial span. Could create duplicate content and double billing if both fragments are charged. Do we have server-side idempotency or resume tokens?

Iris (SRE): Server side currently treats reconnects as new streams unless the client supplies a `stream_resume` header (experimental). The TS SDK doesn't set that header right now. Also server logs for customer show: `stream_open id=abc123 user=cust-789` -> `401 token_expired` -> `token_refresh ok` -> `stream_open id=abc124` -> `partial_chunk seq=42` -> `partial_chunk seq=42` (duplicate).

Jo (DevEx): Oof. Can we get the minimal repro? Also what's the SDK version? We need to avoid umbrella issues with other reconnection modes.

Alex Chen: They are on `@redwood/sdk@0.9.2`. Repro (ts):

```
import Redwood from '@redwood/sdk';
const client = new Redwood.Client({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });

async function run() {
  const it = client.streamCompletion({ model: 'gpt-lite', prompt: 'stream test' });
  let out = '';
  for await (const chunk of it) {
    out += chunk.text;
    // simulate long delay that triggers token rotation
    await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r, 3500));
  }
  console.log('final', out);
}
run();
```

They also provided their auth hook that calls `client.setApiKey(newKey)` on refresh.

Priya Nair: Version 0.9.2 still uses the reconnect path that tries to resume by stitching iterators. We changed behavior in 0.10.x to fetch a resume token from the server, but only when `stream_resume` is enabled. Customer can't enable it.

Samir Patel: Possible fix: on auth refresh we should not silently create a new iterator; instead we should surface an error to the caller (or yield a `__stream_paused__` sentinel) so application code can decide to reopen with idempotency. But breaking change. Alternatively, delay token rotation until open stream completes?

Alex Chen: Customer expects transparent refresh. Their app is long-lived and uses auto-rotate tokens. They reported double billing: they saw two nearly identical charged tokens for the same prompt. Billing trace: `billing_trace: stream.id=abc123 -> charge 0.003` and `billing_trace: stream.id=abc124 -> charge 0.003`. Both show same request fingerprint.

Iris (SRE): We should treat repeated identical fingerprints within a short window as potential dedupe on billing side, but that's a heavier change. Immediate triage: reproduce locally, add unit test that simulates a mid-stream 401 and token swap.

Jo (DevEx): I can try to reproduce on 0.9.2 and 0.10.x. Quick question: is the client-level `setApiKey` synchronous? If it's async and the old connection continues to send events, there might be interleaving.

Alex Chen: It's sync — it just sets the header for subsequent connections. The SDK's reconnect logic does: (1) close old EventSource, (2) create new EventSource with new key, (3) attach a new async iterator and pipe events into the original consumer via an internal queue. That queue is never cleared on reconnect so duplicates can remain.

Samir Patel: OK that's the precise bug: the internal queue semantics + reconnect + token refresh => dupes. Fix path: when creating a new connection, clear internal buffer or attach a new consumer stream instead of piping old buffer. I'll pair with DevEx to ensure behavior across languages.

Jo (DevEx): Repro notes from my local run (0.9.2): I can reproduce ~70% with artificial 401 injection after first partial. Logs:
```
[client] open -> id=abc123
[client] received partial {seq:42, text:"Hello wor"}
[client] injected 401
[client] reconnect -> id=abc124
[client] buffer before pipe:[{seq:42,text:"Hello wor"}]
[client] received partial {seq:42, text:"Hello wor"}  <-- duplicate
```
Iris (SRE): Thanks. Severity? Customer losing data quality + billing. I'd mark P1 for support. Can we propose a mitigation (server-side) while SDK patch is prepared?

Alex Chen: Mitigation idea: server can detect duplicate seq numbers in small windows and drop duplicates for a 10s dedupe window. But there are edgecases when real duplicate is intentional (retries). However could be acceptable as short-term.

Samir Patel: I'll prepare SDK patch: clear internal queue on reconnect and add an opt-in `stream_resume` flag that keeps resume behavior but requires server-side resume tokens. Also add tests to ensure we don't yield duplicates. ETA: branch + PR today, release patch `0.9.3` tomorrow if tests pass.

Jo (DevEx): I'll draft a support reply: apologize, explain root cause (race with token refresh + internal buffer), provide workaround (short term: rotate tokens less frequently during long-running streams OR upgrade to 0.10.x and enable `stream_resume` with server-side support), and promise a patch. Add note about potential billing duplicate and ops will review billing dedupe.

Iris (SRE): I'll open billing review ticket to check whether we can refund duplicate charges and add temporary dedupe on invoicing.

Support Bot: Ticket updated: INC-2026 created, assigned to Samir Patel. Priority P1.

Alex Chen: Action items: Samir (SDK patch + tests), Jo (customer-facing reply + repro asked), Iris (billing triage + short-term dedupe), Priya (coordinate release notes). I'll follow up with the customer once we have a patch or a clear workaround.

Priya Nair: One more ask — can we add an explicit log line in SDK when a reconnect was triggered due to `401` so customers can more easily correlate? Small change and helps debugging.

Samir Patel: Good call. I'll add `console.warn('[redwood-sdk] stream reconnect due to auth refresh')` and include metadata (oldId/newId).

Alex Chen: Thanks everyone. I'll keep this thread updated. If anyone finds additional evidence of server-side duplicate emission please paste logs here.

Jo (DevEx): FYI I opened a quick PR for the queue-clear approach: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1245 (draft). Comments welcome.
